title: Equivalent Fractions, Lowest Terms and Adding Fractions
seo_title: Equivalent Fractions and Adding Fractions – Primary 4 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find equivalent fractions; reduce fractions to their lowest terms; add and subtract fractions with the same and different denominators. (summary of the NERDC Primary 4 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 4 maths worksheets on equivalent fractions, reducing to lowest terms, and adding and subtracting like and unlike fractions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Multiply or divide top and bottom by the same number
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Equivalent fractions have the same value: 1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6. Multiply or divide the numerator and denominator by the same number.
  • To reduce to lowest terms, divide the numerator and denominator by their HCF.
  • Like fractions (same denominator): add or subtract the numerators and keep the denominator. Unlike fractions: first change them to the same denominator (use the LCM).

Examples

Example

Reduce 12/18

HCF = 6

Answer: 2/3

Example

1/3 + 1/4

LCM of 3 and 4 is 12

4/12 + 3/12

Answer: 7/12

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the denominators2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7, not 5/14.
Changing only the numeratorMultiply both the numerator and the denominator.
Not reducing the answerDivide by the HCF to get the lowest terms.

faq.a: Multiplying top and bottom by the same number is like multiplying by 1.
A denominator both fractions can be written with, usually the LCM.
Yes, give the answer in its lowest terms.

items.q: The rectangle shows 12. The dashed lines cut every part into 3 equal pieces. What fraction is shaded now?
items.e: Now there are 2 × 3 = 6 equal pieces, and 1 × 3 = 3 of them are shaded: 36. The pieces are smaller, but the shaded amount did not change, so 12 = 36.

items.q: Divide the top and bottom of 1012 by 2. Which fraction do you get?
items.e: Divide both numbers by 2: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 and 12 ÷ 2 = 6. So 1012 = 56. The parts are bigger, but there are fewer of them.

items.q: Divide the top and bottom of 412 by 4. Which fraction do you get?
items.e: Divide both numbers by 4: 4 ÷ 4 = 1 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3. So 412 = 13. The parts are bigger, but there are fewer of them.

items.q: Divide the top and bottom of 610 by 2. Which fraction do you get?

items.q: Divide the top and bottom of 75100 by 25. Which fraction do you get?
items.e: Divide both numbers by 25: 75 ÷ 25 = 3 and 100 ÷ 25 = 4. So 75100 = 34. The parts are bigger, but there are fewer of them.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 35?
items.e: Multiply the top and bottom by the same number: 3 × 2 = 6 and 5 × 2 = 10, so 35 = 610. Adding the same number, or multiplying only one number, gives a different amount.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 23?
items.e: Multiply the top and bottom by the same number: 2 × 4 = 8 and 3 × 4 = 12, so 23 = 812. Adding the same number, or multiplying only one number, gives a different amount.
